earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only sociolinguistic surveys and wordlists (Reiman 2001/2002 surveys, de Soveral 1913 vocabulary); no grammar or phonology of Lolo (Mozambique) in the bibliography.

sources.citation: the Internet Archive's index index of SIL Mozambique's former site lidemo.net (687 URLs), held at mare1260/
sources.note: lidemo.net had a pagehttp://lidemo.net/lolo-llb/(snapshot 2013-10-17) but no llb_* document was ever posted (Takwane, Chuwabu and Marenje have grammar-notes PDFs there; Lolo has none). web.archive.org is could not be reached by automated download, so the page itself could not be downloaded.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Lolo language (Bantu)' (redirects to Makhuwa language) and Wikidata Q11006056

Bible for Children, Inc. 2025. When God Made Everything (Jenesesi 1-2) [and six further titles: The Start of Man's Sadness, Noah and the Great Flood, The Birth of Jesus, The Miracles of Jesus, The First Easter, Heaven God's Beautiful Home], Lolo (llb) edition; scripture text (c) 2018 Visao Integral from bible.com/bible/3096 (ILOLO). Winnipeg: Bible for Children. PDF, c. 20 pp. each.
sources.note: Nothing: 6.8 kB of Lolo scripture narrative plus an English colophon; a full-text search for stress/accent tone|tonal|stress|acento = 0; no diacritics of any kind in the Lolo text, so the practical orthography encodes neither tone nor stress nor vowel length.

sources.citation: Visao Integral (Ethnos360 / New Tribes Mission Mozambique; translators Matt & Debi Zook and Lolo co-workers). 2018 [NT record dated 2020]. Mazu Otchena a Mulungu [The Word of God]: the Bible in Lolo (ILOLO) - Genesis, Exodus, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, Ruth, 1-2 Samuel, 1-2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, Isaiah, Daniel, Jonah, Malachi and the complete New Testament, with audio. YouVersion/bible.com version 3096; find.bible LLBLNT 'The Lolo New Testament (Mazu Otchena a Mulungu)', Digital Bible Library.
sources.note: Scripture text and audio only; no introduction on orthography or pronunciation seen on the version page; the orthography (as sampled in M2) marks no tone, stress or length. Text+audio pairing would allow a future acoustic check of penultimate prominence but states nothing.

sources.citation: Guérois, Rozenn. 2015. A grammar of Cuwabo (Mozambique, Bantu P34). PhD thesis, Université Lumière Lyon 2. (copy consulted, chuw1238)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Describes Cuwabo (chuw1238), the closest relative in Glottolog's tree; a full-text search for stress/accent, 'Elolo', 'Morrumbala' = 0 hits, so it says nothing about Lolo and cannot be cited for it.

sources.citation: SIL Mozambique. 2013. 'Lolo [llb]' language page on lidemo.net (Internet Archive copy 2013-10-17).
sources.note: Would confirm whether SIL Mozambique ever produced Lolo orthography/grammar notes (the CDX index suggests none); cheap check once web.archive.org is reachable.

sources.citation: Maho, Jouni F. 2009. NUGL Online: The online version of the New Updated Guthrie List. (copy consulted)
sources.note: Classification only: files Lolo llb under P31C Chirima/Shirima together with Kokola kzn (Glottolog instead puts lolo1261 under Chuwabo). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Zook, Matt & Debi Zook (Ethnos360 / New Tribes Mission, Mozambique). c. 2005-2020s. Lolo Bible translation and church-planting language programme (Ethnos360 story 'The Lolo Bibles Have Arrived!'; Zook, Matt. 2010. 'No magic formula', NTM@work Aug 2010: 21-24, describing two years of full-time Lolo culture and language study from 2005).
sources.note: no phonology content in the two pages read (mission narrative only)

sources.citation: Reiman, Duane. 2002 [title page dated 2001]. Findings from the sociolinguistic survey of the Lolo people. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-001. 44 pp. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing. Contents: Introduction, Purpose, Procedures (SIL/NELIMO 200-word list, RTT, questionnaires), Results (lexicostatistics, Chuwabu/Takwane intelligibility), Conclusion; Appendix B 'Word list data' is a stripped-affix morpheme list in a legacy SIL font with no tone/length/stress marking. a full-text search for stress/accent|accent|tone|penult|length|phonolog gives only irrelevant hits ('participants'). Copied from the mare1260 folder (originally an Internet Archive copy of www.sil.org/silesr/2002/001/); the current sil.org PDF (reapdata/46/10/92/.) is could not be reached by automated do…

sources.citation: Shrum, Jeffery & Margaret Shrum. 2001. Western Zambezia language survey in Mozambique: a sociolinguistic survey of the Manyawa, Takwane, Marenje, Kokola and Lolo peoples of Mozambique. SIL Mozambique Working Papers 2: 1-30 (Portuguese: Ibraimo et al. 1998; Shrum & Shrum 2003, Trabalhos em Curso 2).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only other Lolo-specific primary data (rapid appraisal + Lolo/Valade wordlists); a transcription-conventions note could mention penultimate length or tone. Low odds of a stress statement.

sources.citation: Vinton, James E. & Virginia C. Vinton. 2001. A linguistic survey of the Chuwabu language cluster. SIL Mozambique Working Papers 2: 31-49.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Treats Lolo as a Chuwabu-cluster variety with RTT and wordlist data; may contain transcription remarks; also needed to settle whether Lolo should inherit Cuwabo's prosody description.

sources.citation: de Soveral, Antonio. 1913. Vocabulário português-alôlo-lomué. Boletim da Sociedade de Geographia de Lisboa 31(8/9): 272-282.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Oldest Lolo (Alôlo) record; Portuguese colonial wordlists often mark the stressed syllable with acute/circumflex accents and sometimes state a pronunciation rule; would give at least an implicit stress placement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 reference search, any field = 'Lolo Mozambique' (7 hits) and languoid page lolo1261 (classification Makuwa > Chuwabo > Lolo; only reference used: Reiman 2002 for subclassification)

sources.note: All 7 hits are SIL sociolinguistic surveys (Ibraimo et al. 1998; Shrum & Shrum 2001, 2003; Vinton & Vinton 2001, 2003; Reiman 2002) or a bilingual reader (Contos tradicionais bilingues 2001). Zero grammar/phonology/sketch entries for llb.
